title: The theorem of the base
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
of genus $g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ ([def-pc-genus]). Then the
Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ of
[def-sc-picard-functor] is a disjoint union over $d\in\mathbf Z$ of smooth proper $g$-dimensional $k$-varieties
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, whose $k$-points are the
degree-$d$ invertible modules, and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is an open and closed subgroup
scheme; in particular $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is a proper
smooth group scheme of dimension $g$.

proof.text: By [thm-pc-picard-representable], the fppf Picard functor of $C$ is represented by a group scheme $P$ over $k$; its restriction to affine $k$-schemes is the functor of [def-sc-picard-functor] by [lem-pc-picard-functor-agrees-sc]. Since $C$ is nonempty and smooth over the separably closed field $k$, [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives $p\in C(k)$. Apply [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (1)--(3) with $p$: fibrewise degree is locally constant (equivalently, fibrewise Euler characteristic is $d+1-g$), and $P=\coprod_{d\in\mathbf Z}P_d$ with each $P_d$ open and closed and representing $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$. The degree-zero piece is an open and closed subgroup scheme.

proof.text: Let $F$ be the normalized Picard subfunctor of [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor] using $p$. Its representing open subscheme $W\subseteq H_g:=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{C/k}$ is supplied by [thm-pc-f-representable], while the same $F$ is an open subfunctor of $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k,p}$ by [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor], hence of $P$ because $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k,p}\cong\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ [cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso]. Thus $W$ identifies with an open subscheme $U\subseteq P$. For every field extension $K/k$, an $F(K)$-class has $h^0=1$ and $H^1=0$; [cor-picard-degree-g] gives degree $g$, so $U\subseteq P_g$. Now take any point $t$ of $P_g$ with residue field $K$ and associated invertible module $L$ on $C_K$ (a $K$-point of $P$ is a class in $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k,p}(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ by [cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso]). By [lem-pc-twist] there is a line bundle $L_0$ on $C$ with $L\otimes L_{0,K}\in F(K)$. Its degree is zero because both $L$ and the twist have degree $g$. Translation by the $k$-point $[L_0]$ therefore sends $t$ into $U$, and its inverse sends $U$ to an open neighbourhood of $t$ inside $P_g$. These translates of $U$ cover $P_g$.

proof.text: By [thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1), $H_g$ is smooth of dimension $g$ over $k$. Its open $W$ is smooth of relative dimension $g$, and the isomorphism $W\cong U$ of the previous step gives the same property to $U$. Each translate of $U$ is isomorphic over $k$ to $U$. As those translates cover $P_g$, smoothness and relative dimension $g$ hold at every point of $P_g$ by their local definitions [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof.text: The group scheme $P$ is separated over $k$ by [lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field]; hence its open and closed subscheme $P_g$ is separated. It is locally of finite type because it is smooth by the previous step [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. By [thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1), $H_g$ is proper over $k$. The universal divisor gives $\gamma_g:H_g\to P_g$ by [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism], and [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-surjective] makes it surjective (the inequality $g\geq g$ is automatic). Apply the proper-image result [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] to the surjection $H_g\to P_g$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: properness of $H_g$ gives universal closedness of its structure morphism, and separatedness and local finite type of $P_g$ turn the descended universal closedness into properness of $P_g$.

proof.text: The source $H_g$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-hilb-geometrically-integral], with the hypotheses supplied by the smooth projective geometrically integral curve $C$. For every extension $K/k$, the base change of $\gamma_g$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]; hence $P_{g,K}$ is the continuous image of the irreducible $H_{g,K}$ and is irreducible [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-continuous-image]. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change] (2), $P_{g,K}$ remains smooth over $K$. Cover it by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The restriction to each affine open is smooth, so $A_i$ is a smooth $K$-algebra by the affine-local smoothness criterion in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; [lem-sc-smooth-algebra-reduced-field] makes every $A_i$ reduced. Each local ring of $P_{g,K}$ is a localization of such an $A_i$, and localization preserves the absence of nonzero nilpotents, so $P_{g,K}$ is reduced. Thus each $P_{g,K}$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], in particular $P_g$ is an integral, separated finite-type $k$-scheme, i.e. a $k$-variety.

proof.text: For every integer $d$, [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (4) identifies both $P_d$ and $P_g$ with $P_0$ by translation by the $k$-points $[\mathcal O_C(d p)]$ and $[\mathcal O_C(g p)]$. Hence $P_d$ is a smooth proper integral $k$-variety of dimension $g$, and $P_0$ is a proper smooth group scheme of that dimension. Finally [lem-pc-rational-hyp] gives the hypotheses of [thm-pc-pic-split] for the section $p$; at $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$, its exact sequence and $\operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec}k)=0$ identify $P(k)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. By [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (2), the $k$-points of $P_d$ are exactly the degree-$d$ invertible modules.
